decisions.comparison: value.rs scaled_cmp: p 5^n 2^s against q made exactly while n <= bits(q)/2 (a power of five dividing q has no more), else bounds on 5^n (number.rs pow5_wide, shared with the text's leading digits) refined until they decide; equality is impossible there (5^n > 4^n >= 2^(bits(q)+1) > q). Keeps every order the exact scaling gave: value::tests (20,000 random pairs, convergents of log2 10).
decisions.alignment: number.rs aligned: the smaller operand's bits more than prec + 2 below the larger's top become a sticky bit, and in a difference a borrow; rounds as Go's exact sum does (number::exponent_tests, 160,000 random sums and differences, ties, carries, borrows; OPA's numbers oracle pairs).
decisions.reading: number.rs pow5: Go's unused last squaring left out (1e536870939 to 1e646456992 read as Go reads them); a 5^n past Go's exponents is +Inf there and z over it zero; parser.rs: a literal Go reads as +-Inf is 'number too big' as in OPA (testdata/parse-oracle.json regenerated by scripts/rego/generate parse with OPA v1.14.1).
decisions.integers: number.rs MAX_EXPONENT = 1e5, OPA's parser bound on a number (ast/parser.go parseNumber, v1.14.1, its reason golang/go#11068): Float::int refuses past it ('number too big'), so floor, ceil, round, rem, bits.*, numbers.range*, format_int, units.parse_bytes do; units.parse refuses a Rat past it; bits.lsh checks before shifting (its chosen 2^32-bit MAX_SHIFT gone); time.* keep OPA's 'timestamp too big'. Alternatives measured: logs/bigint-text.log (num-bigint's conversion near n^1.8: 17 ms at 1e5 bits, 23 s at 1e7), logs/opa-behaviour.jsonl (OPA's own cost past the bound), Go's big.Float and big.Rat limits.
decisions.texts: a float's text: the parallel lane's d5707dbca (M524), OPA's byte for byte at any exponent; this branch's bound on texts gave way to it at the merge.
decisions.numbers_range: unbounded by design (D98, M510); fuzz/fuzz_targets/rego-builtins.rs asks it for at most one number per input byte, the count bounded with the port's own Float.

rules.R01: No unwrap, expect, indexing or panicking macros in production (clippy -D warnings with the workspace's denials); exponent arithmetic in i128 with values below 2^67, or checked or saturating; BigUint subtraction only after a > b; no allocation from an exponent's value: a shift is bounded by the precision (alignment), the mantissas (comparison) or MAX_EXPONENT (integers). Found and not fixed (pre-existing on origin/main, reproduced, owed): the sort builtin panics where number_compare's order is not total (results.sort_order).
rules.R02: Sources: OPA v1.14.1 (ast/compare.go NumberCompare, ast/parser.go parseNumber, topdown/arithmetic.go, topdown/builtins/builtins.go), Go 1.26.1 math/big (floatconv.go scan and pow5, ratconv.go SetString's limits), golang/go#11068, num-bigint 0.4.8 (convert.rs, division.rs). OPA's own behaviour measured on the same operands (opa/). Alternatives: Go's big.Float range, its big.Rat limits, float64's range, a lean conversion (M524's Open).
rules.R03: MAX_EXPONENT is OPA's parser bound, chosen by OPA for this cost and measured here against OPA's and num-bigint's costs (D98). scaled_cmp's n <= bits(q)/2 and its first precision are derived in its comment (5^n > 4^n; errors doubling per squaring); the alignment's prec + 2 is derived in aligned's; the harness's one number per input byte comes from its input. Test timeouts (60 s) stand for microseconds of work against hours.
rules.R04: No lifecycle state; refusals are typed (number::Error constants OUT_OF_RANGE, OVERFLOW, TOO_BIG), mapped to builtin errors.
rules.R05: No cache, wait or new interface; one pow5 bound shared by the text and the comparison (pow5_wide).
rules.R06: Focused functions: scaled_cmp, shifted_cmp, aligned, at_exponent; the merge folded two pow5 bounds into one.
rules.R07: Comments carry the derivations and Go's and OPA's names.
rules.R08: Not a performance change; OPA's costs on these operands are recorded, not competed with.
rules.R09: Reproduced live: CI's jobs (logs/ci-fuzz-failures.log) and seven artifacts on this Mac; after: every artifact in 0 ms on Linux.
rules.R10: Before/after, mutants, logs and harnesses here; D98 and PM M525.
rules.R11: One implementation, no platform branch. Tests: macOS arm64; fuzzing: Linux x86_64. Owed: the crate's tests on Linux arm64, Windows and musl (CI's matrix), and the seven-target lint (the coordinator's).
rules.R12: Shared pow5 bounds; no platform code.
rules.R13: int_value's bound check, unreachable, removed; the text bound removed at the merge in favour of the lane that writes OPA's text.
